The '''1983–84 Bundesliga''' was the 21st season of the [[Bundesliga]], the premier football league in [[West Germany]]. It began on 12 August 1983<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=326670 |title=Schedule Round 1 |publisher=DFB |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608084614/https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=326670 |archive-date=8 June 2011 }}</ref> and ended on 26 May 1984.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=327032 |title=Archive 1983/1984 Round 34 |publisher=DFB |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608084704/https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=327032 |archive-date=8 June 2011 }}</ref> [[VfB Stuttgart|Stuttgart]] won the championship. Defending champions, [[Hamburger SV|Hamburg]] finished second. The 1983–84 Bundesliga season holds the record for most goals scored in a Bundesliga season.

==Competition modus==
Every team played two games against each other team, one at home and one away. Teams received two points for a win and one point for a draw. If two or more teams were tied on points, places were determined by [[goal difference]] and, if still tied, by goals scored. The team with the most points were crowned champions while the two teams with the fewest points were relegated to [[2. Bundesliga]]. The third-to-last team had to compete in a two-legged relegation/promotion play-off against the third-placed team from 2. Bundesliga.

==Team changes to 1982–83==
[[Karlsruher SC]] and [[Hertha BSC]] were directly relegated to the [[1983–84 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] after finishing in the last two places. They were replaced by [[SV Waldhof Mannheim]] and [[Kickers Offenbach]]. Karlsruhe and Hertha BSC were eventually joined in demotion by relegation/promotion play-off participant [[FC Schalke 04]], who lost on aggregate against [[KFC Uerdingen 05|Bayer 05 Uerdingen]].

==Season overview==

On the 32nd game day of the season 53 goals were scored in 9 games, marking the highest number of goals ever scored in a single game day of the Bundesliga. The 1983–84 season is also the season in which the most goals of the course of the whole season were scored, 1097 in total.

==Relegation play-offs==
[[Eintracht Frankfurt]] and third-placed [[1983–84 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] team [[MSV Duisburg]] had to compete in a two-legged relegation/promotion play-off. Frankfurt won 6–1 on aggregate and remained in the Bundesliga.
